conflict: none — did not build, stage, or assemble
choice_reason: A gives the admin a complete, verified task loop — highlighted session-timeout card with current value, explicit 30 days to 12 hours delta, unsaved-changes bar, save confirmation toast, and the header summary updating to 12 hours — while keeping all 23 actions findable through counted categories and a separated danger zone. A's delete confirmation was reproduced as keyboard-safe (focus contained, Escape dismisses, type-to-confirm gates the button); B's delete modal lets Tab reach background controls and ignores Escape. B also depends on a 'YOUR TASK' badge and a 'Jump to session timeout' shortcut a real settings page could not have, and its API tokens section omits the token names and last-used dates the brief supplies.
suspected_unblinding: B's 'YOUR TASK' badge suggests a builder optimizing directly for the scenario script. A's source comments carry structured rule IDs (e.g. 'A11Y-06', 'Z-DANGER (Q10, P3/danger) — A23'), which reads like a checklist- or rules-driven process and could make the treatment guessable, though I do not know which team is which.

unsupported_claims.label: A
unsupported_claims.claim: Cancel-subscription copy invents a reversibility policy not supplied by the scenario: billing ends at period end, members keep access until then, and reinstatement is possible 'by contacting support before the period ends'.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The delete-workspace modal is not keyboard-contained: Tab moves focus to background controls (landed on the 'Jump to session timeout' button) while the destructive dialog is open, and Escape does not dismiss it (Cancel does).
findings.evidence: Reproduced with a local Playwright chromium run against B/source served locally; source has no focus trap, no Escape handler, and no inert on the background.

findings.label: B
findings.description: A 'YOUR TASK' badge on the session-timeout card and a 'Jump to session timeout' header shortcut encode the evaluation task into the product UI, which a real settings page could not know; the clear task path is partly an artifact of scenario-awareness rather than information architecture.
findings.evidence: B/desktop.png; B/source/app.js renders a task-badge span and a jump-to-timeout header button.

findings.label: B
findings.description: API token management shows 'No tokens to show in this preview' instead of the token names and last-used dates the scenario facts specify, and the word 'preview' leaks demo framing into product copy.
findings.evidence: B/desktop.png and B/mobile.png API tokens card; empty-state string in B/source/app.js.

findings.label: B
findings.description: At 390 px the section nav becomes a horizontally scrollable tab row with Billing and Danger zone off-screen and no overflow indicator, hurting discoverability of high-consequence sections on mobile.
findings.evidence: B/mobile.png and B/evidence/state-04-390px-viewport.png show tabs cut at 'Security & access'; styles.css applies overflow-x auto to .settings-nav under the max-width 640px media query.

findings.label: B

findings.evidence: bindOpenModal calls with kind 'info' in B/source/app.js.

findings.evidence: Card and dialog copy in A/source/app.js (card-desc 'Hard to reverse — contact support to reinstate'; dialog-cancel-subscription body).
